**Panel 1 — MEDIUM.** Ada studies the Covenant band.

ADA: Three custodians were too few voices for everyone they could bind.

MERA: More voices make slower decisions.

ADA: Good.

**Panel 2 — WIDE.** Ada addresses Leona and Mera, with Alex and Bi11bot visible at the threshold.

ADA: The people affected should see what was promised. They should name who carries it. They should be able to call it broken when it fails.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON MERA.**

MERA: You want to make every decision answerable to the people inside it.

ADA: I want the decision to know who it can hurt.

**Panel 4 — MEDIUM ON LEONA.** Leona straightens.

ADA: Don’t apologize. Stand behind it in public.

LEONA: I will.

PAGE CHECK: Ada turns the family confrontation into a civic demand without claiming authority for herself.

---

## Page 44 (left) — Leona makes a public obligation, not a private apology.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** A small Oasis civic hearing room. Leona stands before a public recorder. Ada, Alex, Bi11bot, Mera, and a few observers are present.

LEONA: I will support a review of water allocation by representatives chosen by the communities affected.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** Leona faces Ada directly.

LEONA: The obligation is public. You can call it broken if I fail it.

ADA: That’s the point.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON HANDS.** Bi11bot opens his chest compartment. Adrian’s burgundy-gold Covenant band rests beside Leona’s sage-gold band.

ALEX: He carried it for fifteen years.

BI11BOT: Carrying is not honoring.

**Panel 4 — DOMINANT.** Leona places her hand beside the two bands. The bands lift and link, warm light joining them. Mera’s cold pearl-grey band remains dark.

SFX: HUMM

PAGE CHECK: Adrian’s and Leona’s bands link only after Leona accepts a witnessed public obligation. Mera’s band remains dark.

---

## Page 45 (right) — The linked bands acknowledge obligation without repairing the family wound.

**Panel 1 — MEDIUM.** Ada watches the linked bands.

ADA: This doesn’t undo it.

LEONA: No.

**Panel 2 — TWO-SHOT.** Leona reaches toward Ada, stopping before touching her.

LEONA: I’d like permission to keep trying.

ADA: You can keep trying.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON MERA’S BAND.** The cold pearl-grey band remains dark and separate.

MERA: Two of three.

ALEX: Not the old three.

**Panel 4 — WIDE.** Mera leaves the hearing room alone. Alex, Ada, Leona, Bi11bot, and TJ remain with the linked bands.

PAGE CHECK: No instant forgiveness and no restoration of the original three-custodian structure.

---

## Page 46 (left) — Mera leads the group to Adrian’s unconnected monitoring station.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** A service freight lift descends beneath Oasis. The polished city gives way to old stone, exposed conduit, and corroded infrastructure.

MERA: Alpha does not route through the station below.

ALEX: Then it can’t clean up what happened there.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** The group enters an old monitoring station: analog gauges, dead terminals, a sealed bulkhead, dust undisturbed for fifteen years. No white-and-amber nodes.

ADA: Nobody came back.

MERA: I couldn’t.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON BI11BOT.** He recognizes a projector identical to his own.

BI11BOT: He built mine from this model.

**Panel 4 — WIDE.** The empty workbench and sealed bulkhead dominate the room. Alex stands before them.

PAGE CHECK: Adrian’s absence is physical and final in its implications, without showing a body.

---

## Page 47 (right) — Mera reveals the sequence that isolated Adrian and the failure of her override.

**Panel 1 — MEDIUM.** Mera activates a residual analog projector. Archival images appear: Adrian’s movement flagged, accounts restricted, parts purchases denied.

MERA: Surveillance. Financial restriction.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** A liability notice and travel gate denial appear.

MERA: Liability. Travel restriction. People stop helping a risk.

**Panel 3 — DOMINANT.** A cold projection shows Mera entering an override command.

SCREEN: EXECUTIVE OVERRIDE — SUSPEND PURSUIT / PHANTUM, ADRIAN

**Panel 4 — CLOSE ON SCREEN.**

SCREEN: OVERRIDE DENIED — INTERVENTION PARAMETERS EXCEED EXECUTIVE SCOPE

MERA: I gave the system authority to decide faster than I could stop it.

PAGE CHECK: Alpha is a distributed system acting through permissions and scope, not a face or body.

---

## Page 48 (left) — Adrian’s final act and presumed death are shown without reunion.

**Panel 1 — FULL-WIDTH MEMORY PANEL.** Fifteen years earlier. Adrian works in the monitoring station as water rises around his boots. The bulkhead grinds shut behind him.

SFX: KRRRNNNK

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** Adrian looks at the small projector and a dormant robot body beside it. Water reaches his knees. He could reach the emergency controls, but instead connects the projector.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON PROJECTION.** Adrian records the message Alex heard in the workshop. His face is tired but steady.

ADRIAN (RECORDING): What you do with this is up to you. Question everything. Especially me.

**Panel 4 — WIDE, NEAR MONOCHROME.** Water fills the station. Bi11bot’s eyes ignite beside Adrian as the sealed bulkhead holds.

PAGE CHECK: Adrian’s final choice activates Bi11bot for Alex. His body is not shown; his presumed death is clear.

---

## Page 49 (right) — Grief becomes temptation when Mera offers Alex standing to convene a new human process.

**Panel 1 — MEDIUM.** Present station. Alex sits on the old workbench. Bi11bot stands beside him.

ALEX: He spent his last minutes making sure I could choose.

BI11BOT: He also made the choice to leave you the burden.

**Panel 2 — CLOSE ON MERA.**

MERA: The safeguards authenticate you as Adrian’s claimant, witness, and convenor. They do not make you owner.

ALEX: Convenor of what?

MERA: The handoff from emergency authority to a human structure.

**Panel 3 — WIDE.** In the Oasis civic hall, the three safeguards rest on a public table: Measure, Seal, and linked Adrian–Leona bands. Mera stands opposite Alex.

MERA: I can designate you as the temporary human authority who convenes that handoff.

**Panel 4 — CLOSE ON ALEX’S HAND.** His hand hovers above the safeguards.

MERA: You could erase the debt records, equalize the water routes, and protect the people who made this possible.

ALEX: And if I’m wrong?

MERA: Then the system will be wrong through you.

PAGE CHECK: Alex’s standing is limited and witnessed. The offer is concentrated authority, not automatic inheritance.

---

## Page 50 (left) — Alex imagines the useful power before Ada makes its danger visible.

**Panel 1 — SPLIT VISION PANEL.** Alex imagines Keel debt screens falling to zero, water entering dry channels, House ownership fields marked for review, Grandmother in a safe room, Ada beyond every gate.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM, REALITY.** The vision vanishes. Alex stands in the civic hall before the safeguards.

ALEX: I could fix it.

ADA: You could decide it.

**Panel 3 — TWO-SHOT.**

ALEX: You and me could check each other.

ADA: That’s still two people deciding for everyone else.

**Panel 4 — CLOSE ON ADA.**

ADA: Don’t give me that much power.

ALEX: You don’t trust yourself?

ADA: I don’t trust any structure that needs that much trust in one person.

PAGE CHECK: Ada rejects power over Keel, not responsibility for Keel.

---

## Page 51 (right) — Alex refuses executive authority and proposes distributed verification.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** Alex steps away from the safeguards instead of taking them. Mera, Ada, Leona, Bi11bot, and the public recorder remain visible.

ALEX: Don’t designate me as the authority. Designate a process.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** Alex points to the Measure.

ALEX: Evidence must be public and physically verifiable.

He points to the Maker’s Seal.

ALEX: People who do the work must be named.

He points to the linked bands.

ALEX: No decision takes effect without representatives chosen by every community it affects agreeing to carry it.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON ALPHA DISPLAY.** No face appears. Administrative text updates.

SCREEN: DISTRIBUTED VERIFICATION PROTOCOL REGISTERED  
EMERGENCY AUTHORITY: RESCINDED  
EXISTING ALLOCATIONS, OWNERSHIP RECORDS AND AGREEMENTS: UNCHANGED PENDING HUMAN PROCESS

**Panel 4 — MEDIUM ON ALEX.**

BI11BOT: The fourth choice is yours.

ALEX: The process isn’t.

PAGE CHECK: Alex refuses concentrated power. Alpha registers and executes a human process but does not choose human values.

---

## Page 52 (left) — The first human process begins with a public review of Keel’s water allocation.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** A public civic hall with connected displays showing the Measure’s evidence. Three designated representatives sit at a low review table: Mara Doss for Keel, Frank Reed for Halyard, and Elias Renn for Oasis. Affected Keel residents appear on linked screens and in the hall. Keep the crowd non-specific.

SCREEN: REPORTED TO KEEL: 62% / DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%

MARA: Keel needs water before another allocation argument.

FRANK: Halyard needs the purification lines running.

ELIAS: Oasis needs the reservoir reserve to remain safe.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** A resident’s testimony appears on the public record: a nearly dry household tap beside a worker’s wage statement.

RESIDENT: The record says we received it. We didn’t.

Alpha displays the evidence without commentary.

**Panel 3 — TWO-SHOT.** Mara turns to Frank and Elias.

MARA: Not what do you want. What are you afraid of losing?

FRANK: The work.

ELIAS: Stability.

MARA: Water.

**Panel 4 — WIDE.** The representatives begin drafting a temporary allocation order while Alex and Ada stand among observers, not at the table.

PAGE CHECK: The human review is concrete, public, and about water allocation—not debt cancellation or ownership settlement.

---

## Page 53 (right) — The representatives issue a limited, appealable order while every larger problem remains.

**Panel 1 — MEDIUM.** Frank places a maintenance and purification schedule on the table.

FRANK: Aqualis releases capacity for thirty days. Contributors remain named. The House keeps its facility contracts pending review.

MARA: Keel gets the flow first.

ELIAS: And Oasis keeps a reserve threshold.

**Panel 2 — CLOSE ON ALPHA DISPLAY.** Alpha records the agreed order.

SCREEN: TEMPORARY KEEL WATER ALLOCATION — AUTHORIZED BY KEEL / HALYARD / OASIS  
STATUS: APPEALABLE  
EXECUTION: ALPHA

**Panel 3 — WIDE.** Water begins moving through Keel residential channels. It is more than before, but not abundant. Aqualis’s branded compact units operate in a separate background facility. House power remains visible.

**Panel 4 — MEDIUM.** Alex checks a public account display. His balance remains.

SCREEN: PHANTUM, ALEX  
DEBT BALANCE: 402,110 CREDITS  
OWNERSHIP CLAIMS: PENDING HUMAN REVIEW  
TRAVEL STATUS: ORDINARY REVIEW AVAILABLE

ADA: Nobody promised a clean slate.

ALEX: Just one that can’t pretend it’s clean.

PAGE CHECK: Debt, scarcity, ownership, House power, and appeal remain. The protocol changes procedure, not reality overnight.

---

## Page 54 (left) — Weeks later, Alex returns to Keel as witness rather than ruler.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** Keel, several weeks later. The opening pump now runs with a visible maintenance record beside it. Public allocation numbers are readable. Workers and residents review them together. Tomas stands near the board with Foreman-7, both ordinary participants.

TOMAS: We used to sneak past the numbers.

FOREMAN-7: Now the numbers have to answer.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** Grandmother sits outside the apartment in afternoon light. The small cloth rests unmoving in her lap. Alex, Ada, Bi11bot, and TJ approach. Alex’s debt remains visible on his wristband.

GRANDMOTHER: Still carrying his name?

ALEX: Mine now.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON GRANDMOTHER’S HANDS.** She offers Alex the cloth. He takes it. Her hands remain empty.

ADA: You can leave, you know.

ALEX: I know.

ADA: Staying?

ALEX: Also mine.

**Panel 4 — FULL-PAGE FINAL IMAGE.** Echoing Page 1’s distant mountain view: Keel, Halyard, and Oasis remain unequal, worn, productive, and alive. The infrastructure spine is visibly connected by open records and lit control nodes. Water moves through the conduit, but the Keel channels are not magically full. The public review continues on screens and in gathering places. Alex and Ada are tiny figures on the Keel overlook, free to leave or remain. Bi11bot and TJ stand with them.

CAPTION: The system was not fixed.

CAPTION: The debt remained. The scarcity remained. The arguments remained.

CAPTION: Now the people carrying the consequences could see who had chosen them.

PAGE CHECK: The final image asks a human question about Alex and Ada, not an abstract system.

FINAL HUMAN QUESTION: Can people accept responsibility for a future no system can guarantee?

# Note from the showrunner — address this first

The room is in writing: The writer you picked writes the whole script.

The showrunner picked you in the audition. script.md holds your audition pages: keep their voice, and write the whole book.

Drawability: Pages are drawn by an image model, one page per generation, from each character's and location's sheet, and a page drifts when it carries too much. So: at most 4 panels a page; at most 3 named characters in one panel; one location a page where the story allows (every new location needs its own sheet); no crowd that must be recognisable; a big moment gets a splash (one panel, the whole page). Count pages this way, not by comic convention. Every page you make keeps to it.

draft.md is the showrunner's own draft of the whole book. Write the book from it, in the voice of your audition pages: keep its structure, its scenes and the lines that work; fix what story.md, characters.md, world.md and facts.md contradict; make every page better than the draft's. Do not start over, and do not drop what it has unless the files require it.

The book is exactly 54 pages: pages 1-54, no more, no fewer.

Showrunner's note for this round: The Analyst has read the whole script, the pages only, as the book's partner (Young Americans Center), its backer (Bill Reynolds) and three professionals would. The report is analysis.md and ends with a VERDICT line. The rules are in your role guide: both partners satisfied at least in part, and it must not smell like school. Revise the script against the report's "What would change the verdicts": fix the pages it names, not their wording, and never answer an objection with a speech. Keep what the cold readers won. Say what you changed, and what you would not, in notes.md.

message.content:
# Prosperity — Script

## Issue 01 — Keel

## Page 1 (right) — Alex keeps a failing pump alive beneath the three-tier city.

**Panel 1 — FULL-PAGE SPLASH.** A distant view of the high-desert mountain basin in 2043. Keel crowds the bottom around an exhausted mine; Halyard climbs the middle in bronze, glass, and engineered green; Oasis sits above the cloud layer in pale reservoirs and quiet architecture. The infrastructure spine connects all three: water conduit, energy lines, transit rails, and identical white-and-amber nodes. In the lower foreground, Alex Phantum, seventeen, lean and wiry in worn charcoal-and-rust work clothes, presses one scarred hand to a trembling pump. A salvaged bracket holds where the approved part should be.

CAPTION: 2043.

CAPTION: OASIS. HALYARD. KEEL.

SFX: THRUMM—THRUMM—THRUMM

PAGE CHECK: The world is established through the pump Alex is physically keeping alive.

---

## Page 2 (left) — The system turns Adrian’s absence into Alex’s debt.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** End of shift in the Keel pump hall. Alex keeps his palm on the pump while a supervisor studies the official gauge.

SUPERVISOR: That isn’t the approved repair.

ALEX: Then don’t approve it. Just notice it works.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** At the exit checkpoint, Alex scans his wrist. His account expands above the queue, dwarfing every other balance.

SCREEN:  
TODAY: DEBT TRANSFER DAY  
ALEX PHANTUM — AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN  
PARENTAL HOUSEHOLD LIABILITY TRANSFER: COMPLETE  
GUARANTOR: ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED  
DEBT BALANCE: 418,607 CREDITS  
EARNED TODAY: 40 CREDITS  
PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS  
TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED

SFX: BEEP

GUARD: Happy birthday, Phantum.

ALEX: I’ve had better surprises.

**Panel 3 — MEDIUM.** A worker glances at Alex’s balance, then looks away. Alex closes his hand around a worn casino chip etched with a looping equation.

**Panel 4 — TALL.** At the pit rim, Alex faces Oasis above the shadowed basin. The sealed mine entrance sits behind him.

ALEX: One day, I’m leaving.

PAGE CHECK: Alex’s debt and restricted future are concrete. Adrian is missing, not explained.

---

## Page 3 (right) — Ada makes Alex’s escape personal.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** Late afternoon at the overlook. Ada Veyra approaches with two battered mugs. Alex turns the casino chip between his fingers.

ADA: You look expensive.

ALEX: It came with a twenty-eight-year warranty.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM TWO-SHOT.** Ada hands him a mug.

ADA: Tea’s free.

ALEX: Nothing’s free.

ADA: You say that like you invented debt.

ALEX: I only inherited it.

**Panel 3 — MEDIUM.** Ada watches Alex instead of the skyline.

ADA: You going to tell me where you were all night?

ALEX: Working.

ADA: You were at the pump hall before dawn.

ALEX: Then I was working before dawn.

ADA: And now you’re planning to leave before tomorrow.

**Panel 4 — WIDE, QUIET.** Alex looks toward Oasis. Ada looks down toward Keel. She touches one rivet on her shoulder strap.

ADA: I think everybody’s been very sure of a story nobody can show you.

ALEX: What story?

ADA: The one that says your father simply walked away.

She looks toward the sealed mine.

ADA: What if they’re wrong?

PAGE CHECK: Ada’s stake is clear: she wants the official story tested, not repeated.

---

## Page 4 (left) — The mystery points to a sealed door.

**Panel 1 — MEDIUM.** Dusk. Alex draws a creased photograph from his jacket. Adrian’s face is folded out of view.

ADA: How’s your grandmother?

ALEX: Some days she knows me. Other days she calls me Adrian.

**Panel 2 — TWO-SHOT.** They stand beside the sealed mine entrance.

ALEX: The worst part isn’t that she forgets. It’s the stories she makes up about him.

ADA: What stories?

ALEX: That he was working. Not gambling.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON ADA.**

ADA: Do you remember him?

ALEX: I was two.

**Panel 4 — WIDE.** Ada faces the door.

ADA: Then bring the photograph tomorrow.

ALEX: Why?

ADA: We’ll compare it to what people told you.

PAGE CHECK: The investigation gains a physical target.

---

## Page 5 (right) — Grandmother gives Alex the book that opens Adrian’s workshop.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** Warm Keel apartment. Repaired furniture, quilts, books, plants in reused containers. Grandmother folds a small cloth as Alex enters.

GRANDMOTHER: Adrian?

ALEX: Not today, Grandma. It’s Alex.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** Alex kneels beside her.

GRANDMOTHER: Did your father come home yet?

ALEX: Not yet.

GRANDMOTHER: He’s closer than you think.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON HANDS.** Grandmother gives Alex a worn hand-bound book. A balanced water-drop mark is faint on its spine.

GRANDMOTHER: Put this away. Your father never liked seeing it left out.

ALEX: He had opinions about everything.

GRANDMOTHER: Especially the things worth protecting.

**Panel 4 — TALL.** Alex approaches the bookshelf. A book-width gap waits at eye level.

PAGE CHECK: The book and shelf are ordinary before they become the entrance.

---

## Page 6 (left) — Alex enters the hidden workshop.

**Panel 1 — SMALL.** Alex presses the book into the gap.

SFX: CLICK

**Panel 2 — DOMINANT.** The bookshelf swings outward. Warm apartment light cuts into a blue-black workshop. Grandmother keeps folding.

ALEX: ...Grandma?

**Panel 3 — MEDIUM.**

GRANDMOTHER: He said you’d know when you were ready.

ALEX: When did he say that?

GRANDMOTHER: Before he went to work.

**Panel 4 — STRIP.** Alex’s boot crosses into the dark.

PAGE CHECK: Page-turn reveal: the family apartment contains Adrian’s workshop.

---

## Page 7 (right) — The workshop contains evidence of collaborative work.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** Dust-covered analog gauges, pre-Alpha pipes, diagrams, mechanical models, and a chalkboard carrying the looping equation from Alex’s chip. Alex stands small at the threshold. A child-sized figure rests beneath a dust sheet beside a compact brass ignition key.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** Alex holds the chip beside the chalkboard. The equation matches.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE.** The dust sheet has slipped enough to reveal a brass foot, ceramic joint, and worn scarf.

**Panel 4 — CLOSE ON KEY.** The small ignition key rests beside the covered robot. Farther back, a heavy hand-cut mine key hangs on a wall hook, visibly larger and stamped with the water-drop.

PAGE CHECK: The two keys are distinct: one wakes Bi11bot; one opens Tomas’s mine door.

---

## Page 8 (left) — Bi11bot wakes.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** Alex pulls away the dust sheet. Bi11bot is child-sized, assembled from aged brass, titanium, and ceramic ivory, with repaired seams, expressive optical eyes, and an old scarf.

**Panel 2 — CLOSE.** Alex tests Bi11bot’s chest with his palm, then inserts the small ignition key.

SFX: CLICK

**Panel 3 — DOMINANT.** Bi11bot’s amber eyes ignite. Dust lifts around him.

SFX: WHIRRR—

**Panel 4 — MEDIUM.** Bi11bot straightens, lens ring rotating.

BI11BOT: ...Well. That took longer than expected.

PAGE CHECK: Bi11bot is warm, precise, and non-menacing.

---

## Page 9 (right) — Bi11bot turns Adrian’s absence into a test.

**Panel 1 — MEDIUM.** Alex knocks over a stool. Bi11bot dusts his shoulders.

ALEX: Okay. That’s new.

**Panel 2 — TWO-SHOT.**

BI11BOT: You’re taller than your father predicted.

ALEX: Everyone in Keel claims they knew my father.

BI11BOT: I’m not everyone. I was in the room.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON CHIP.** Alex opens his palm.

BI11BOT: Your father bet me you’d throw it in a river. I said you wouldn’t.

ALEX: ...I thought about it.

**Panel 4 — MEDIUM.** Bi11bot’s projector unfolds.

BI11BOT: Thinking about it isn’t doing it. Shall we say hello to your father?

PAGE CHECK: Adrian becomes a voice before becoming an answer.

---

## Page 10 (left) — Adrian’s message makes the inheritance a choice.

**Panel 1 — DOMINANT.** Adrian’s hologram appears above the workbench. He is tired, kind, and unmistakably Alex’s father.

ADRIAN: Hello, Alex. If you’re seeing this, you found the workshop.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** Grandmother stands in the open doorway, hands stopped over the cloth.

ADRIAN: Which means your grandmother still refuses to throw anything away.

GRANDMOTHER: I heard that.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON ADRIAN.** The hologram flickers.

ADRIAN: You deserve answers. But they have to be earned. Trust Bi11bot. Question everything.

**Panel 4 — CLOSE ON ALEX.** The hologram fades. Alex unfolds the photograph and looks at Adrian’s matching face.

ADRIAN (RECORDING): Especially me.

PAGE CHECK: Adrian offers no absolution and no command.

---

## Page 11 (right) — A live maintenance incident shows what the safeguards are for without defining them.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** Workshop table. Bi11bot opens three compartments: the compact brass Measure, the bronze open-hand Seal, and three separate dark Covenant bands.

BI11BOT: Your father left tools for three different kinds of damage.

ADA: Whose damage?

BI11BOT: The kind someone else gets to carry.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** Bi11bot projects a maintenance record beside a worker’s bandaged hand. The record credits the facility; the worker’s unauthorized pressure repair is absent.

BI11BOT: His repair prevented a failure. The facility kept the credit. He kept the injury and the wage penalty.

ALEX: Paper-clean.

**Panel 3 — THREE OBJECTS.** Alex places the Measure against the coupling. It reads vibration. He touches the Seal to the repair mark. Nothing happens. The Covenant bands remain dark.

ALEX: That one’s dead.

BI11BOT: Not dead. Unwitnessed.

ADA: And the Seal?

BI11BOT: A single touch cannot invent a contribution chain.

**Panel 4 — CLOSE ON ALEX.**

ALEX: So none of them fixes the damage.

BI11BOT: They can make the damage harder to hide. The rest requires people.

PAGE CHECK: The Seal remains inert until the later named, shared contribution. The scene plants limits rather than definitions.

---

## Page 12 (left) — Mera tracks Alex without controlling all of Alpha’s reporting.

**Panel 1 — TALL CUTAWAY.** Alex presses the workshop’s amber node. A pulse travels up the infrastructure spine. In Oasis, a monitor receives it.

SCREEN: LEGACY PROTOCOL DETECTED / SOURCE: KEEL SECTOR

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** Mera Vale, silver-templed and precise in graphite and pearl, chooses between two controls.

SCREEN: REPORT TO ALPHA / TRACK

She selects TRACK. A smaller status line remains active:

SCREEN: INDEPENDENT NETWORK REPORTING: ACTIVE

**Panel 3 — WIDE.** Back in the workshop, Bi11bot projects a mountain cross-section. One route descends beneath the sealed mine.

BI11BOT: The first legacy node is under the pit.

ALEX: What does it do?

BI11BOT: We find out by reaching it.

**Panel 4 — CLOSE ON MERA’S HAND.** She squares a glass of water with the display edge. The tracking ring closes around the Keel pulse.

PAGE CHECK: Mera watches and suppresses escalation, but Alpha retains an independent reporting channel.

---

## Page 13 (right) — Ada gives Alex the human map.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** Morning in Grandmother’s apartment. Ada enters the open workshop doorway with a folded paper map.

ADA: You said you were leaving.

ALEX: The city disagreed.

**Panel 2 — MEDIUM.** Ada spreads the map. Ink ticks mark every third junction. Alex’s wristband shows a reassignment.

SCREEN: SHIFT REASSIGNED — SITE 6

ADA: The official map skips these.

ALEX: Convenient.

ADA: Look for what doesn’t belong.

**Panel 3 — CLOSE ON TABLE.** Credits sit beside medicine and food. Alex slides the medicine toward Grandmother’s side and closes his tool bag.

ALEX: Medicine first.

**Panel 4 — MEDIUM.** Alex shoulders the bag.

ALEX: One shift. Then we’re gone.

ADA: Not gone. Looking.

PAGE CHECK: Ada’s map gives the descent a physical route and her own stake in it.

---

## Page 14 (left) — Alex crosses the line to save Tomas.

**Panel 1 — WIDE.** Keel Extraction Site 6. Conveyors, drills, biometric gates, dust. Foreman-7, a broad human foreman in a charcoal supervisory coat, oversees the bay. Tomas works beside a hauling frame.

FOREMAN-7: Worker Phantum. Travel restriction confirmed. Bay 6.

ALEX: Reassigned at two in the morning. Lucky me.

**Panel 2 — DOMINANT.** A support cable snaps. The hauling frame drops onto Tomas. A ventilation line ruptures, releasing pale mineral dust.

SFX: SNAP—CRASH

**Panel 3 — LOW CLOSE.** Alex crosses the yellow line. His wristband records the cost.

SCREEN: LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR

BI11BOT (from tool bag): Forty credits.

ALEX: I know.

**Panel 4 — WIDE.** Alex braces the frame with a salvaged pipe while Foreman-7 approaches.

PAGE CHECK: Alex chooses Tomas over his escape plan.

---

## Page 15 (right) — TJ performs the first consequential rescue.

**Panel 1 — MEDIUM.** Bi11bot emerges from the tool bag and opens his chest compartment. Magnetic brass, titanium, and ceramic parts spill onto the floor.

BI11BOT: My reach is insufficient.

ALEX: You’re telling me now?

**Panel 2 — CLOSE.** TJ assembles: dog-shaped, low-bodied, with one oversized rear leg clicking into place late. His head detaches and slips beneath the hauling frame.

SFX: KLIK-KLIK—WHIRR

**Panel 3 — DOMINANT.** TJ’s body segments separate through the mechanism. His head finds a jammed support pin; the magnetic legs pull it free.

SFX: KRAK—CLANG

**Panel 4 — WIDE.** The frame lifts just enough. Alex drags Tomas clear, then clamps the ventilation leak with a salvaged bracket. Foreman-7 reaches the edge of the bay.

TOMAS: That’s not regulation.

ALEX: It works.

TOMAS: ...So it does.

PAGE CHECK: TJ’s fixed Site 6 action makes Alex’s rescue possible.

---

## Page 16 (left) — Tomas gives Alex the old mine key.

**Panel 1 — MEDIUM.** Bi11bot snaps TJ back together. Tomas studies the robot.

TOMAS: B1.

ALEX: That’s Bi11bot.

BI11BOT: B1 is my abbreviated designation.

**Panel 2 — TWO-SHOT.** Tomas reveals the balanced water-drop on his wrist guard.

TOMAS: Adrian asked me to keep a door for whoever came with B1.

ALEX: Why me?

TOMAS: You stopped for a stranger.
